item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00201","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C11","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's treatment of public officials. Its compact list of officials exempted from voluntary-induction classification closely matches the child's distinctive list of Ready Reserve members presumptively transferred to the Standby Reserve, including the Vice President, governors, legislators, judges of courts of record, and other statewide elected officials. Both provisions also use a written voluntary commitment as a mechanism for retaining or entering the more immediately available military category. C11 and C20 contain broader classification machinery paralleling several child criteria—fitness, civilian occupation, hardship, officials, and reserve status—but their correspondence is less concentrated and direct than C25's official-by-official list.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The following elective and appointive officials: (1) The Vice President of the United States; members of the Cabinet and other Presidential appointees requiring Senate confirmation. (2) The Governors... (3) Members of the legislative bodies... (4) Judges of the courts of record... (5) All other officials chosen by the voters of an entire state, Territory or possession.","parent_excerpt":"He is the Vice President of the United States, a Governor of a State, any other State official chosen by the voters of the entire State, a member of the Congress of the United States, a member of a State legislative body, or a judge of a court of record of the United States or of a State, required to be deferred by law.","explanation":"This is a distinctive, substantially coextensive enumeration of public offices, not merely shared military-service subject matter."},{"child_excerpt":"shall be transferred to the Standby Reserve unless they execute a written agreement to remain in the Ready Reserve for a minimum period of one year","parent_excerpt":"Registrants... may volunteer at their local board for induction... by filing an Application for Voluntary Induction","explanation":"Both schemes make individual written election the means of entering or remaining in the category more immediately available for service, although the exact form and duration differ."},{"child_excerpt":"Members... whose call to active duty in an emergency would result in extreme personal or community hardship... [and those] principally engaged or employed in critical civilian occupations","parent_excerpt":"Disregarding all other grounds for deferment, he would be classified in Class II-A, Class II-C, or Class III-A","explanation":"The referenced classifications concern occupational and dependency-based deferments, paralleling the child's adjacent hardship and critical-civilian-occupation screening criteria and reinforcing the structural relationship."}]}
